messages:
Support: @eng-sre heads up — customer 'AcmeCorp' opened ticket #12345 reporting a regression in tail latency on /v1/generate starting ~03:20 UTC. p50 ~50ms, p95 ~300ms, p99 spiking to ~1.1s. They say sudden after a deploy. Requesting triage.

Linh Tran: Copy of the customer repro: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-1\",\"input\":\"short prompt\"}' — they sent 100 parallel requests and attached a small flamegraph + logs.

Maria Gomez: Thanks @Linh. Looking at grafana (https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abc/route-latency?from=now-1h). I can see p99 jump exactly at 02:55 UTC. Deploy history shows a config change to continuous-batcher defaults at 02:50 (PR #3582).

Ajay Patel: that PR bumped default hold_ms from 10 -> 60 and max_batch_size from 16 -> 64 to improve throughput for high-volume customers. It looks like it rolled to canary and then 100% by 02:52. Link: https://git.redwood/infr/PR/3582.

Devin O'Connor: Ugh — that explains it. For low concurrency hotpaths, increasing hold_ms increases p99 because requests wait for batch fill. Customer's traffic is spiky so longer hold adds queue latency.

Maria Gomez: Repro steps from Acme match. They run many small parallel requests (short tokens) so batch never fills quickly. We need immediate mitigation: rollback or route override to previous batching profile.

Ajay Patel: Proposed quick fixes: 
- route-level override for /v1/generate to set hold_ms=10 and max_batch_size=8
- or roll back global change to 10ms while we evaluate
Either is quick. I can push a route override in console.

Maria Gomez: Route override is lower blast radius. Please also mark the change as emergency canary if you touch infra.

Ajay Patel: Executing route override now. Command I will run: 
```
redwoodctl set-batcher-config --route "/v1/generate" --hold-ms 10 --max-batch 8 --reason "emergency: p99 regression for AcmeCorp"
```

deploy-bot: deployment queued: set-batcher-config for route "/v1/generate" by ajay (ID: dpl-89734).

Maria Gomez: Also add `eager_flush: true` for that route so single-request fast paths don't wait.

Ajay Patel: applying with eager_flush. New config snippet: 
```
{
  "route": "/v1/generate",
  "batcher": {
    "hold_ms": 10,
    "max_batch_size": 8,
    "eager_flush": true
  }
}
```

deploy-bot: deployment started dpl-89734 -> rolling to 12 nodes.

metrics-bot: rule triggered: route:/v1/generate p99 decreased from 1.12s -> 0.27s within 90s of dpl-89734. (See panels: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abc/route-latency?from=now-15m)

Linh Tran: Customer confirmed improvement in their next test run: "much better, p99 ~250ms now". They asked what changed.

Maria Gomez: Summary for support: we applied a route-level batcher override (hold_ms=10, max_batch_size=8, eager_flush=true) to restore low-latency hotpath behavior. Root cause: global change to continuous-batcher defaults increased hold window to favor throughput, which regresses tail latency for low-concurrency short requests.

Devin O'Connor: Short-term mitigation done. Next actions: 
- Ajay: open a follow-up PR to make default adaptive (auto-lower hold_ms for routes with short-avg-reqs) — owner @Ajay.
- Maria: run an offline sim against Acme traffic pattern to propose route templates and add test to perf-suite.
- Linh: update customer ticket with explanation & CA.
- Oncall: monitor p99 for other routes for 24h and alert if similar spikes.

Ajay Patel: Created follow-up issue #3897: "Adaptive batcher defaults + route templates" and assigned to eng-runtime. Linking to PR for reversible config DSL.

Maria Gomez: Also capturing this in postmortem draft. Note: consider defaulting `eager_flush` to true for routes with median token length < 16 and request-rate < X.

Linh Tran: I'll tell Acme we're keeping the override and will follow up with timeline for the adaptive change. They asked for a patch ETA — I'll give a conservative 2-week window.

Maria Gomez: Great. Closing this thread once tickets created and follow-ups assigned. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
